responses: He's Broken. His mind is damaged in a way I don't fully understand. Mad though he may be, he has insights that sometimes help us, sometimes harm us.
He brings things, people, and it is usually a fifty percent chance that it turns out bad for us.
So, that's the chance I'll give. I have with me an old Septim, a coin, tarnished on one side, much like your empire outside.
I will flip it, and if it lands on the unsullied side, you may stay. Otherwise, you will find your home in the equations below.
Seems Sotha Sil smiles on you today, outsider. Let us hope he does the same for us. Now, speak freely, outlander, or go away.

full_name: Llavados said I can help you with a serious problem that you're having.

parent_topic_full_name: Llavados said I can help you with a serious problem that you're having.
responses: I can see his logic, however twisted. But he didn't tell you what was the problem, did he?
That's not his style. He's not good with words. Or speaking, or handling machinery. He broke the Upgate on his way out, for one thing.
I am better at explaining, so let me try.
We are Chronographers, fabricant servants of the god Seht. We monitor time and space and stop it from collapsing in on itself.
One of the ways we do so is by overseeing the Towers. This particular Tower that we sit under is Snow-Throat, known as the Throat of the World.
The towers are one of the most essential mechanisms of the world, the pinpoints of the Wheels of Lull, yet one by one, they are slowly dying.
For years, we have watched the most essential pieces of Snow-Throat, but now it starts to flicker and fade, and we don't know why.
If Snow-Throat has been deactivated or is at risk of such, it is a serious threat, not just to our order, but to Nirn as a whole.
(The FRF gives you a note and a teleport ball, then trundles off.)
